display_name: John, disciple of Gregory the Decapolite

names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 18 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan, ucenicul Sfântului Grigorie Decapolitul».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 18 April, „Преп. Јован.“, with Преп. left off, which is the venerable this folder already carries in `types`. **The heading is a rank word and a bare forename and nothing else** — the discipleship this corpus keeps in his display name is the body's first sentence, not the heading's — so there is no fuller form to store. Six folders already hold this bare Serbian form; this is a seventh, and the fold is recorded as deliberate in the run's findings.

Read out of the title on the name link behind his place in the line for 11 апреля ст. ст., name page 1018, «Иоанн Солунский (Фессалоникийский), прп.», with the rank word left off. The day’s own line gives the name in the genitive. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports the stored form as a key no other folder holds. The second epithet is kept in the brackets the calendar prints it in; the bare «Иоанн» was refused, because the plain gate already folds ten folders onto the Serbian «Јован» of which this one is a member.

feast.note: His life page on the same site heads «Дни памяти: 11 апреля , 18 апреля» and keeps both. This row stands on 11 апреля, the day whose page listed him; 18 апреля is the day the `romanian` and `greek` rows already on this folder carry, and the difference is seven days and not the thirteen of the style conversion, so the two are two commemorations. One row per church is the schema, so the eighteenth is recorded here and he does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 11 апреля ст. ст. — «Прп. Иоанна , ученика прп. Григория Декаполита (IX).»
source.note: The line names him only as the disciple of his teacher and gives a century, «(IX)»; the name link behind it gives him Thessalonica twice over, in both of the Russian adjectives for the city. The life page behind the line is the fullest account of him this corpus has read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 18 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan, ucenicul Sfântului Grigorie Decapolitul»

attestations.note: Not checked: saint.gr for 18 Απριλίου (20 September 2026).

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.05.2026 (18. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Јован.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian keeps him on; the Greek row stays `undocumented`. The identification is not on the name, which is bare: the entry's first words are that he was the disciple of St Gregory the Decapolite, and it then names the iconoclast emperor Leo the Armenian and Joseph the Hymnographer, who buried him near Gregory's grave — the same three men, in the same relation, as the Romanian life this folder was written from. **The year is new to this folder**: „Скончао мирно око 820. год.“, about 820, where the Romanian notice says in so many words that no year is given anywhere in it. Two things are new besides, and both are differences rather than additions: that the emperor **put John to the torture together with his teacher Gregory and with Joseph the Hymnographer**, where the Romanian life has the three of them walking about the city strengthening the Orthodox and does not say they were tortured; and that **after Gregory's death John became abbot of the Decapolite's monastery in Constantinople** and redoubled his labour as abbot, which is why `abbot` was added to `types`. Both readings stand and neither was chosen. **No `office`** was added: that would be a key in all four locale packs and the monastery's name is not this folder's to mint. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Cu curgerile lacrimilor tale ai lucrat pustiul cel neroditor şi cu suspinurile cele dintru adânc ai făcut ostenelile tale însutit roditoare; şi te-ai făcut luminător lumii, strălucind cu minunile, Ioan, părintele nostru. Roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Ioan, ucenicul Sfântului Grigorie Decapolitul», Glasul 8

english.text: With the streams of your tears you worked the barren desert, and with sighs from the depths you made your labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and you became a light to the world, shining with wonders, John our father. Pray to Christ God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Воздержанием, отче, житие украсив,/ и плоть умертвил еси,/ темже и победил еси вражия прилоги, преблаженне,/ и прешел еси к Богу/ в безскорбный и вечный живот,/ яко достоин наследник, Иоанне,// Емуже молися спастися нам.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 11 апреля ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Иоанна», глас 4, under «Молитвы»
source.note: It names this saint and no other, so it is his own proper and not a hymn mis-hung from a neighbour on the day. Copied out of the page by `.tmp/ru0411/hymns.py` rather than retyped.

english.text: Adorning thy life with abstinence, O father, thou didst put the flesh to death, and so didst overcome the assaults of the enemy, O most blessed one, and didst pass over to God into a life eternal and without sorrow, as a worthy heir, O John. Pray to Him, that we may be saved.

birth.note: days.pravoslavie.ru’s life: «Преподобный Иоанн родился в конце VIII века» — born at the end of the eighth century. The folder held no birth date; the bounds are the last quarter of that century and nothing narrower is stated. Read 7 October 2026.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue for 18. април ст. ст.: „Скончао мирно око 820. год.“ — he reposed peacefully about 820. days.pravoslavie.ru agrees by way of his teacher: it dates Gregory’s repose «около 820 года» and says «вскоре за ним отошел ко Господу и его верный ученик Иоанн», soon after him his faithful disciple John departed to the Lord. Neither page gives John a year of his own, so the reading is unchanged. Read 7 October 2026.
